text: Putnam's multiple realizability argument is standardly directed against which thesis, and on what grounds?
choices: Against eliminative materialism, on the grounds that folk-psychological posits fail to map onto neural kinds.
Against substance dualism, on the grounds that an immaterial mind could not be realized in matter.
Against functionalism, on the grounds that one and the same function could not be realized by different physical systems.
Against type-identity theory, on the grounds that a mental type like pain can be realized by different physical state types across species, so it is not identical to any single one of them.
explanation: Multiple realizability attacks type-identity: if octopuses and hypothetical silicon aliens can feel pain without C-fibers, pain is not identical to C-fiber stimulation. Crucially the argument supports functionalism rather than opposing it, so option 2 inverts the actual relation. It is also distinct from the knowledge argument, which targets physicalism via an epistemic premise rather than via facts about realization.
